policy-operation.title: PolicyOperation
policy-operation.description: An operation a policy can guard; the policy catalog lists them.

pol-not_found.description:
Policy: not found

Error code: pol.not_found

pol-permission_denied.description:
Policy: the caller's project role does not allow this operation

Error code: pol.permission_denied

policy-id.description: The identifier of a policy, shared by all of its revisions.

policy-revision-id.description: The identifier of one immutable revision of a policy.

password-set-config.title: PasswordSetPolicyConfig
password-set-config.description:
The settings of an `auth.factor.password.set` policy. Every setting is
optional; a setting left out switches its rule off, and `{}` switches every
rule off. There are no defaults. The bounds are technical limits, not
recommendations; the server's template checks the same bounds.

min_length.description:
The fewest Unicode code points a new password may have, counted after
NFC normalization. At most `max_length` when both are set.

max_length.description:
The most Unicode code points a new password may have. A password above
64 code points is refused whether or not this is set.

history_depth.description:
How many of the user's passwords a new one may not repeat, the current
one included. Checked only when users set their own password.

password-set-policy.title: PasswordSetPolicy
password-set-policy.description:
One revision of a project's `auth.factor.password.set` policy (ADR 066).
`id` is shared by every revision of the operation's policy; `revision_id`
names this revision.

project_id.description: The project the policy belongs to.

created_at.description: When the operation's policy was first published.

policy.title: Policy

list-policies-response.description:
Paginated list of the project's policies, one per operation, each as its
newest revision.

next_page_token.description:
Token to pass as `page_token` in the next request to fetch the following
page. Absent when there are no more results.

password-set-policy-input.title: PasswordSetPolicyInput
password-set-policy-input.description: A publish of the password policy, checked before a password is set.

publish-policy-request.title: PublishPolicyRequest
publish-policy-request.description:
One publish of the project's policy for an operation. `operation` selects
the operation's template, and `config` sets that template's settings; a
setting left out is off, and `{}` switches every rule off. The settings each
operation accepts are listed in the policy catalog.

pol-revision_conflict.description:
Policy: another revision of the same policy was published at the same instant; retry

Error code: pol.revision_conflict

password-set-evaluate-input.title: PasswordSetEvaluateInput
password-set-evaluate-input.description:
The password as a user or administrator would set it. The server derives
what the policy checks (its length in code points after NFC normalization)
with the same code a password set runs.

password.description:
The candidate password. It is evaluated and dropped: never stored,
logged or returned. Anything above the server's cap of 64 characters is
refused as `max_length`, as on a real set; the 4096 bound only keeps a
dry run's body small.

password-set-evaluate-facts.title: PasswordSetEvaluateFacts
password-set-evaluate-facts.description:
What a password set looks up instead of reading from the request. A dry run
has no user, so it is stated here.

self_service.description:
Whether the user sets their own password. Only then is the password
history checked; an administrator's set skips it.

history_matches.description:
Whether the candidate matches each of the user's kept passwords,
current first, newest first. Only the first `history_depth` entries
count, so at most 4, the highest `history_depth`.

password-set-evaluate-request.title: PasswordSetEvaluateRequest
password-set-evaluate-request.description: A dry run of the password policy for one candidate password.

evaluate-policy-request.title: EvaluatePolicyRequest
evaluate-policy-request.description:
One dry run of an operation's policy. `operation` selects the operation's
template; `config` is the policy to evaluate, checked exactly as a publish
checks it; `input` is what the operation's request carries, in the
operation's own terms; `facts` states what the operation would look up at
runtime. The fields each operation accepts are listed in the policy
catalog.

evaluate-policy-response.title: EvaluatePolicyResponse
evaluate-policy-response.description:
The decision the operation would reach for the request. A refusal carries
the error code and violations an API call of the operation would answer
with; a login flow shows the same rules as field errors instead.

allowed.description: Whether the operation would go ahead.

code.description:
The error code an API call of the operation would answer with, set
only when it would refuse, for example `user.password_empty` or
`user.password_policy_violation`.

violations.description:
Every failed rule keyed by name with the value of the setting it is
named after, e.g. `{"min_length": 12}`, as the live error's
`details.violations`. Set only with `user.password_policy_violation`.

list-policy-revisions-response.description: Paginated list of the revisions of one policy, newest first.

next_page_token.description:
Token to pass as `page_token` in the next request to fetch the following
page. Absent when there are no more results.

release-content-hash.title: ReleaseContentHash
release-content-hash.description:
The content digest of a release: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex
characters. Always the full digest; no short form is accepted anywhere.

The digest covers the content of the resources the release pins and
nothing else. Revision ids, metadata and the project are not part of it.
A bundle that carries every resource it references therefore has the same
digest on every project, and a client can compute it before sending
anything. When a bundle leaves a referenced resource to the project, the
release pins the project's revision of it too, and the digest covers that
resource as the project holds it.

To compute it:

1. Take every resource in the release as the `bundle` of
   `POST /releases/build` carries it, with `kind` set to `schema`,
   `flow_definition`, `branding` or `idp`, and `handle` set to the
   schema's `objectType`, the flow definition's `name`, `default` for
   branding, or the IDP connection's `slug`.
   A `schema-url` entry's content is the entry as written, and its handle
   is the `objectType` of the document the URL serves.
2. Build the JSON document
   `{"version": 1, "resources": [{"kind": …, "handle": …, "content": …}, …]}`,
   with `resources` sorted by `kind`, then by `handle`.
3. Serialise that document as canonical JSON (RFC 8785).
4. The digest is the SHA-256 of those bytes, written as `sha256:` and
   lowercase hex.

A release built from `pointers` has the digest its pinned revisions would
have if they were sent as a bundle.

The digest identifies a release on the wire but never appears in a path,
which takes the `rel_` id. Fields that look a release up by content say
so by name: the `content_hash` filter of `GET /releases`, and
`content_hash` in place of `release_id` on `POST /deployments`.

rel-permission_denied.description:
Release: requires an operator-grade token bound to the project (project.write or a release.* scope)

Error code: rel.permission_denied

release-id.description: The opaque, immutable identifier of a release.

release-metadata.title: ReleaseMetadata
release-metadata.description:
Who assembled the release, when, and from what source. Set when the release
is assembled and never mutated afterwards.

message.description:
A short caller-supplied summary of what the release changes, analogous to
a git commit message.

git_sha.description:
The source commit the caller was operating from. Recording it on both
releases is what lets two releases be diffed at field level in the
source repository they were built from.

git_dirty.description:
True when the working tree had uncommitted changes at construction time.
`git_sha` still points at HEAD, but the release content does not
correspond to that commit exactly, so consumers of the git-diff mechanism
should skip it when either side is dirty.

created_at.description: When the release was assembled.

created_by.description:
The identity that assembled the release. Absent when the caller is a
machine principal carrying no user identity, which is the common case for
releases constructed from CI or the CLI.

release-summary.title: ReleaseSummary
release-summary.description:
A release without its pinned set — the shape `GET /releases` returns.

Pointers are omitted rather than optional so that a list entry can never be
mistaken for a release that pins nothing; fetch them with
`GET /releases/{release_id}`.

id.description: The opaque, immutable resource id, assigned at construction.

project_id.description: The project this release belongs to.

content_hash.description: The digest of the pinned content.

revoked_at.description: When the release was revoked, or null while it is not.

next_page_token.description:
Token to pass as `page_token` in the next request to fetch the following page.
Absent when there are no more results.

release-pointer-kind.title: ReleasePointerKind
release-pointer-kind.description:
The kind of resource a release pointer pins.

Carried explicitly rather than inferred from `revision_id`, because a
revision id is not always shaped distinctly enough to identify its kind: a
schema's is its `$id`, which may be any URL.

`flow_definition` rather than `flow`: a release pins the definitions served
at `/flow_definitions`, not the runtime flows at `/flow`.

create-release-pointer.description:
One revision to pin. The handle is not supplied: it is the resource's own
identifying field, so the server reads it from the revision being pinned and
records it on the release.

revision_id.description:
The revision of that resource to pin. Must already exist in the project —
this endpoint pins revisions, it does not create them.

Deliberately not constrained to a prefixed id: for `kind: schema` this is
the schema's `$id`, which is a URL whenever the document supplied one and
only a generated `sch_*` value otherwise.

create-release-request.description:
The set of revisions to bundle into a release, plus the metadata to record
alongside it.

`created_at` and `created_by` are derived server-side from the caller's
authentication context and are not accepted here.

pointers.description:
The revisions to pin. Must not be empty.

A kind usually appears more than once: a project has several user schemas
and several flow definitions, and each is pinned on its own. What it
cannot do is
pin two revisions of the *same* resource — a second revision of the
`human-user` schema is rejected rather than ordered, since a release
describes one state of the project.

The upper bound counts *resources*, not revisions — one release pins at
most one revision of each — so it is a limit on how much a project
configures, not on how often it changes. It keeps the server's
per-pointer revision lookups bounded by the contract rather than by the
request, and is set conservatively: raising it is a spec change, and
widening a bound breaks no client that was already inside it.

message.description:
A short summary of what the release changes, analogous to a git commit
message. Recorded on the release and shown when listing releases.

git_sha.description: The source commit the caller was operating from.

git_dirty.description:
Set when the working tree had uncommitted changes, so the release content
does not correspond exactly to `git_sha`.

rel-project_not_found.description:
Release: project not found

Error code: rel.project_not_found

rel-revision_not_found.description:
Release: pinned revision does not exist

Error code: rel.revision_not_found

rel-revision_unpinnable.description:
Release: pinned revision declares no handle

Error code: rel.revision_unpinnable

rel-unresolved_reference.description:
Release: handle is not in the release

Error code: rel.unresolved_reference

release-pointer.description:
One entry of the set a release pins: the revision of a single resource that
this release includes.

handle.description:
Which resource this pointer pins, independent of which revision of it.
`revision_id` chooses the revision; `handle` says what the revision is a
revision *of*. Determined when the release is assembled, not supplied by
the caller:

- `schema` — the document's `objectType`, so `human-user` and
  `machine-user` are separate resources a release pins separately
- `flow_definition` — the definition's `name`, likewise for
  `default-login` and `b2b-login`
- `branding` — always `default`. A project has one branding, so there is
  nothing to distinguish; it is revisioned like everything else, and
  `revision_id` is what varies between releases.
- `idp` — the connection's `slug`, so `google` and `github` are
  separate resources a release pins separately
- `policy` — the policy's `operation`, so a project's password policy
  is one resource however often it is revised

Resources inside a release reference each other by handle rather than by
revision id, so the same handle names the same resource in every release.

revision_id.description:
The revision of that resource this release pins.

Deliberately not constrained to a prefixed id: for `kind: schema` this is
the schema's `$id`, which is a URL whenever the document supplied one and
only a generated `sch_*` value otherwise.

release.title: Release
release.description:
An immutable, project-scoped snapshot that pins one revision of every
resource it includes.

A release owns pointers and metadata, not content — it records *which*
revisions belong together. Callers that need the resource bytes resolve each
`revision_id` through the per-kind read endpoints (`GET /schemas/{id}`,
`GET /flow_definitions/{id}`, …).

A release exists on its own and is not tied to an origin. Deploying it is a
separate call.

Two identifiers: `id` is the one paths and `release_id` fields take;
`content_hash` is the digest of the content the release pins, printed by
the CLI and pinned by builds, and looked up through fields that name it.

id.description: The opaque, immutable resource id, assigned at construction.

project_id.description: The project this release belongs to.

content_hash.description:
The digest of the pinned content. Identical for two releases with the
same content, which is why a project never holds two such releases.

revoked_at.description:
When the release was revoked, or null while it is not. A revoked
release cannot be deployed and is refused on every path that would
serve it, including to a build that pins its digest. No origin serves
a revoked release, since a release an origin still serves cannot be
revoked; earlier deployments that named it stay in the history.

pointers.description:
The revisions this release pins, one entry per `(kind, handle)`. Never
empty: a release must contain at least one resource, and never longer
than the set `POST /releases` accepts.

configuration-bundle.title: ConfigurationBundle
configuration-bundle.description:
The resources of a project's `.zitadel/` directory as authored on disk,
grouped by kind.

Resources reference each other by handle: a flow definition's
`user_schema` names a schema by its `objectType`, and a flow step's
`sso_providers`, like a schema's `x-auth-methods.sso.providers`, name IDP
connections by `slug`. A reference resolves to
the resource with that handle in this bundle; failing that, to the
project's newest revision of it, which the release then pins as well. A
handle that neither holds refuses the release, naming the pointer and the
handle. A bundle that references only resources it carries builds the
same release on any project.

A handle names one resource of its kind in a bundle. Two schemas with the
same `objectType`, two flow definitions with the same `name`, two IDP
connections with the same `slug`, two policies for the same `operation`,
or a schema without an `objectType` refuse the release with `rel.invalid`,
with an entry for each such resource.

Each kind is optional, and the arrays may be empty: a project that never
ejected its branding omits `branding`. The bundle carries at least one
resource, and the release it builds pins at most 50, the most a release
pins: the resources the bundle carries plus those resolved from the
project. The server refuses anything outside that with `rel.invalid`.
Unknown keys are refused. More kinds join as they become release kinds.

schemas.description:
User schemas, one per `.zitadel/schemas/*.json`, in either form
`POST /schemas` takes.

An inline `user-schema` must not declare `$id`: a schema's `$id` is
its revision's identity, so a changed schema under the same `$id`
could never become a new revision. Such a schema gets a `rel.invalid`
entry.

A `schema-url` entry's handle is the `objectType` of the document the
URL serves. Its revision is identified by the URL, so the release
reuses the project's revision for a URL the project already holds and
fetches the document only for a URL it does not.

idps.description:
IDP connections, one per `.zitadel/idps/<slug>.json`, each the
connection document `POST /idps` takes as `idp`. Secrets appear only
as `${{ NAME }}` references to variables, never as values, so a bundle
carries no credentials.

policies.description:
Operation policies, one per `.zitadel/policies/<operation>.json`, each
the body `POST /policies` takes. The handle is `operation`: a project
has one policy per operation. An unknown setting or a value outside a
setting's bounds is refused while the request is decoded, with
`req.invalid` and no `details.resources`; a config the operation's
template refuses beyond that, such as settings that contradict each
other, gets a `rel.invalid` entry.

A request served this release reads the policy revision it pins for
the operation, as it reads the user schema, branding and identity
providers, once the release pins a flow; a release that pins a flow
and no policy for an operation means no policy for it.

branding.description:
The descriptor from `.zitadel/branding/branding.json` with its template
inlined, exactly as `POST /branding` takes it. A project has one
branding, so this is a single object.

build-release-request.title: BuildReleaseRequest
build-release-request.description:
The resources to build a release from, plus the metadata to record
alongside it.

`created_at` and `created_by` are derived server-side from the caller's
authentication context and are not accepted here.

message.description:
A short summary of what the release changes, analogous to a git commit
message. Recorded on the release and shown when listing releases.

git_sha.description: The source commit the caller was operating from.

git_dirty.description:
Set when the working tree had uncommitted changes, so the release content
does not correspond exactly to `git_sha`.

bundle-resource-error.title: BundleResourceError
bundle-resource-error.description:
One bundle resource that failed validation: the error its kind's create
endpoint would have answered, `code`, `message` and `details` unchanged,
with the resource it belongs to.

index.description: The resource's position in its kind's array in the bundle; `0` for the branding.

handle.description: The resource's handle, when it declares one.

build-release-bad-request.title: BuildReleaseBadRequest
build-release-bad-request.description:
The bundle cannot build a release. `code` says why. A structurally
malformed request, such as a wrong type, a missing required field, an
unknown key or a kind over its cap, is refused while decoding with
`req.invalid`, naming the offending fields. A well-formed bundle whose
resources fail the checks their kinds' create endpoints run answers
`rel.invalid`, and `details.resources` lists every resource that failed.

The handler returns this response directly, with `resources` at the top
of `details`, rather than through the shared error path, which would nest
a producer's payload under `details.details`.

resources.description: Every bundle resource that failed validation.

rel-in_use.description:
Release: still served by an origin

Error code: rel.in_use

deployment-id.description: The opaque, immutable identifier of a deployment.

revoke-release-conflict.title: RevokeReleaseConflict
revoke-release-conflict.description: The release cannot be revoked because origins still serve it.

origins.description: Every origin that still serves the release.

deployment_id.description: The newest deployment to the origin, which pins the release.

user-locator.title: UserLocator
user-locator.description:
Name a user with exactly one of `user_id` or `identifier`. Sending both
or neither is `grant.invalid`. Unknown properties are rejected by
`additionalProperties: false` as `req.invalid` before the handler runs.

user_id.description:
Platform-homed user id (`user_<opaque>`). The user must be active.
Granting the session caller's own user id is `grant.invalid`.

identifier.description:
The user schema's designated identifier (`x-identifier`), looked
up in the platform project. Create answers 202 with no body on
every outcome: a hit, a duplicate, a miss, and several matches are
indistinguishable, and a miss or several matches write nothing.
The server logs the lookup outcome. Granting the session caller's
own resolved user is `grant.invalid`.

team-locator.title: TeamLocator
team-locator.description:
Name a team with exactly one of `team_id` or `name`. Sending both
or neither is `grant.invalid`. Unknown properties are rejected by
`additionalProperties: false` as `req.invalid` before the handler runs.

team_id.description: Platform-homed team id (`team_<opaque>`). The team must be active.

name.description:
Team name, unique per project case-insensitively. Looked up in
the platform project. The team must be active.

create-grant-request.title: CreateGrantRequest
create-grant-request.description:
Bind a user or a team. Exactly one of `user` or `team`. Shared fields are
`relation` and optional `expires_at`. Sending both locators or neither is
`grant.invalid`.

relation.description: Catalog relation on `object_type` `project`. `team` (owning-team) is not allowed.

expires_at.description:
Optional expiry. Must be in the future when set. Expiry stops
authorization but does not free the unique binding; DELETE the grant
before posting the same principal and relation again.

user.description:
User to bind. Exactly one of `user_id` or `identifier`. The user must
exist in the platform project when a platform project is configured.
Mutually exclusive with `team`.

team.description:
Team to bind. Exactly one of `team_id` or `name`. The team must exist
in the platform project when a platform project is configured.
Mutually exclusive with `user`.

grant-already_exists.description:
An unrevoked grant with this principal and relation already exists on the project

Error code: grant.already_exists

grant-invalid.description:
The grant request is invalid

Error code: grant.invalid

grant-not_found.description:
Grant not found

Error code: grant.not_found

grant-permission_denied.description:
Insufficient permissions to manage grants

Error code: grant.permission_denied

grant-principal_not_found.description:
The principal could not be resolved

Error code: grant.principal_not_found

grant-user.title: GrantUser
grant-user.description:
User bound by this grant. Always a user-ref (`user_id`, never `id`).
`expand: ["principal"]` adds the User envelope fields `schema`,
`attributes`, and `metadata` on this same object. Missing users degrade to
`user_id` only, with or without expand (ADR 059 grant exception).

schema.description:
The schema that defines `attributes`. Present only when the request
asked for `expand: ["principal"]` and the user could be loaded.

attributes.description:
Present only when the request asked for `expand: ["principal"]` and
the user could be loaded.

metadata.description:
Server-owned user envelope. Present only when the request asked
for `expand: ["principal"]` and the user could be loaded. Grant
expand does not populate `lifecycle_owner_team`.

grant-team.title: GrantTeam
grant-team.description:
Team bound by this grant. Always a team-ref (`team_id`, never `id`).
`expand: ["principal"]` adds `status`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` on
this same object. Missing teams degrade to `team_id` only, with or without
expand (ADR 059 grant exception).

status.description:
Team lifecycle. Present only when the request asked for
`expand: ["principal"]` and the team could be loaded.

created_at.description: When the team was created. Present only when expand loaded the team.

updated_at.description: When the team was last updated. Present only when expand loaded the team.

grant.title: Grant
grant.description:
A collaboration grant binding a user or a team to a project relation.
Discriminate on which of `user` or `team` is present. Those objects are
always refs (`user_id` / `team_id`); expand adds extra fields on the same
object rather than a sibling.

id.description: Managed assignment id (`asgn_<opaque>`).

project_id.description: Project this grant is scoped to.

object_type.description: Catalog object type. Always `project` for this API.

created_at.description: When the grant was created.

expires_at.description:
When the grant expires. Null when it does not expire. GET still
returns expired unrevoked grants; authorization ignores them.

user.description:
Present on a user grant. Omit on a team grant. Always a user-ref
(`user_id`); expand adds envelope fields on this same object.

team.description:
Present on a team grant. Omit on a user grant. Always a team-ref
(`team_id`); expand adds envelope fields on this same object.

grant-expand.description:
Ask for extra fields on the bound user or team. Those extras land on
`user` or `team` themselves; there is no sibling `principal` object.

`principal` adds `schema`, `attributes`, and `metadata` on `user`, or
`status`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` on `team`. The id (`user_id` /
`team_id`) is always present. If the user or team cannot be loaded, the
object stays id-only — the same shape as not expanding.

Expanding requires `user.read` and `team.read` in addition to
`project.read` for project secrets. Both are checked once for the whole
request. If the caller lacks either, the request is 403; extras are not
omitted silently. A user-bound Console session that already passed the
project Check may expand without those scopes.

grant-sorting-field.description:
Field to sort grants by. Default is `created_at` ascending with `id` as
the tiebreaker.

grant-filter-field.description:
Field to filter grants by:
- `created_at`: RFC3339 timestamp
- `user_id`: user principal id (`user_<opaque>`)
- `team_id`: team principal id (`team_<opaque>`)
- `relation`: `viewer`, `editor`, or `admin`
- `expires_at`: RFC3339 timestamp (null when the grant does not expire)

query-grants-request.description: Request to query the grants of a project.

page_token.description:
Token to retrieve the next page of results. Must be sent with the same
`sorting` as the request that issued the token. Omitting `sorting` reuses
the default sort and only succeeds when that default matches the token.

expand.description:
Extra principal fields to add onto each grant's `user` or `team`
(ADR 059 grant exception). Omit it and those objects stay refs. An
unrecognised value is rejected.

filter.description: Filter criteria for querying grants. Combined with AND.

next_page_token.description:
Token to pass as `page_token` in the next request to fetch the following page.
Absent when there are no more results. The follow-up request must repeat the
same `sorting` that produced this token (omit only when both pages use the default).

evt-not_found.description:
Event: not found

Error code: evt.not_found

evt-permission_denied.description:
Event: permission denied

Error code: evt.permission_denied

event-metadata.description:
Emit-time metadata, already redacted at write. Path A request.api may
set client (ip, user_agent, origin) for SIEM join on request_id. Not a
live risk-evaluator input.

authorization.description:
What authorized the request, when it was not a grant on the event's
project (ADR 053 §8). Every event of such a request carries it.

path.description:
`platform_operator`: the deployment's platform operator relation
(ADR 075), which administers every project.

actor_home_project_id.description: The project the actor's user belongs to.

client.description: Observed HTTP requestor context on Path A request.api only.

ip.description: Client IP from the first X-Forwarded-For hop or RemoteAddr.

event-base.description:
Shared wide-event envelope (ADR 048 / ADR 049). Concrete events are
`allOf` this schema plus a `const` `event_type` and a typed `payload`.

id.description: Managed event id (`evt_<opaque>`).

team_id.description: Emit-time team scope, when the actor operated under a team.

event_type.description:
Semantic event name (dot-separated). Discriminator for the Event union —
see docs/design/api/events-catalog.md.

occurred_at.description: When the action happened (server/storage clock, dialect-owned).

created_at.description: When the row was inserted (server/storage clock, dialect-owned).

token_id.description: Token id present at emit time, when any.

empty-event-payload.title: EmptyEventPayload
empty-event-payload.description:
Empty payload for event types with no typed fields
(e.g. `project.deleted`, `user.deleted`, `session.expired`).

auth-check-payload.title: AuthCheckPayload
auth-check-payload.description:
Payload for `auth.check.failed` / `auth.check.succeeded`,
`auth.sso.authorization.failed`, and `auth.sso.exchange.failed` /
`auth.sso.exchange.succeeded`.
`auth_attempt_id` joins the check to its attempt for SIEM correlation.

deployment-created-payload.title: DeploymentCreatedPayload
deployment-created-payload.description:
Allowlisted fields for `deployment.created`. The deployment id is already
the event's `entity_id`; the fields here say what went live where.

targets.description: The origins the release went live on, sorted.

flowdef-payload.title: FlowdefPayload
flowdef-payload.description:
Allowlisted fields of the created revision. Retired `flowdef.updated`
rows carry a delta in the same shape. Steps are omitted.

idp-payload.title: IdpPayload
idp-payload.description:
Shared allowlisted fields for `idp.created` (snapshot) and `idp.updated`
(delta: only changed fields present, plus the new `revision_id`). The
connection id is the event's `entity_id`. The connection document, and with
it the `client_secret` reference, is never included.

template.description:
The rendering template hint. On `idp.updated`, the empty string means
the revision removed it.

idp-identity-link-created-payload.title: IdpIdentityLinkCreatedPayload
idp-identity-link-created-payload.description:
Snapshot for `idp.identity_link.created`, written when a sign-in creates a
user and links the provider account to it. The link id is the event's
`entity_id`. The provider's subject and claims are never included.

connection_id.description: The IdP connection the account signed in through.

user_id.description: The user the provider account is linked to.

policy-payload.title: PolicyPayload
policy-payload.description:
Allowlisted fields for `policy.created` (the first publish of an
operation's policy) and `policy.updated` (every later publish). The policy id
is the event's `entity_id`. `config` holds the published settings, which are
configuration values, never user data.

operation.description: The operation the policy guards, e.g. `auth.factor.password.set`.

project-payload.title: ProjectPayload
project-payload.description:
Shared allowlisted fields for `project.created` (full snapshot) and
`project.updated` (delta: only changed fields present).

password_hash_algorithm.description:
The password hashing algorithm the project switched to. The empty string
means it was handed back to the server default. Absent when the update
did not touch hashing.

release-created-payload.title: ReleaseCreatedPayload
release-created-payload.description:
Allowlisted fields for `release.created`. The release id is already the
event's `entity_id`; the pinned set is repeated here so the audit stream
answers what a release contained without reading the release itself.

release-revoked-payload.title: ReleaseRevokedPayload
release-revoked-payload.description:
Allowlisted fields for `release.revoked`. The release id is already the
event's `entity_id`; the digest is repeated so the audit stream names the
release the way the CLI prints it and builds pin it.

schema-created-payload.title: SchemaCreatedPayload
schema-created-payload.description:
Allowlisted fields for `schema.created`. The schema document itself is
omitted — it is customer-authored and unbounded, and the event's `entity_id`
already identifies which schema was created.

kind.description:
The kind the stored document declares. `unknown` when the schema was
persisted without its document being parsed.

object_type.description:
The customer-chosen object type the schema describes. Absent when the
document declares none.

team-payload.title: TeamPayload
team-payload.description:
Shared allowlisted fields for `team.created` (snapshot) and
`team.updated` (delta: only changed fields present).

user-created-payload.title: UserCreatedPayload
user-created-payload.description:
Payload for `user.created`. Identity is `entity_id`; attribute values
appear only for schema fields marked `x-audit`.

user-updated-payload.title: UserUpdatedPayload
user-updated-payload.description:
Payload for `user.updated`. Same attribute rules as create: keys touched
plus `x-audit` values only.

variable-removed-payload.title: VariableRemovedPayload
variable-removed-payload.description: Payload for `variable.removed` events, one row removed.

variable-set-payload.title: VariableSetPayload
variable-set-payload.description:
Payload for `variable.set` events: one row entered or replaced. The value
is never included, plain or encrypted.

event.description:
Discriminated wide-event union (ADR 048 / ADR 049). Clients select the
member via event_type; each member carries a typed payload.

next_page_token.description:
Token to pass as `page_token` in the next request to fetch the following page.
Absent when there are no more results.

variable-kind.description:
Which deployments a value reaches: `primary` for primary origins,
`preview` for preview URLs. There is no fallback between kinds.

var-not_found.description:
Variable: not found

Error code: var.not_found

var-permission_denied.description:
Variable: permission denied

Error code: var.permission_denied

variable-name.description:
A variable's name, unique per project and kind.

Word characters only, which is exactly what the `${{ NAME }}` reference
syntax can address: a name outside that grammar could be stored
but never referenced from a configuration document.

variable-scalar.title: VariableScalar
variable-scalar.description:
A variable's value. JSON scalars only — a string, a number, or a boolean.

The value travels through JSON in both directions, so the set of types is
JSON's. A number always reads back as a JSON number however it was written;
a type JSON has no scalar for (a timestamp, say) is rejected rather than
quietly coming back as the string it serialized to. Strings are capped at
16 KiB: a variable is a configuration value, not a payload.

secret-variable.title: SecretVariable
secret-variable.description:
A secret, on the way out. It says that a value is held under this name and
that the value is secret; it never carries the value itself.

A secret is stored encrypted and reads back as ciphertext, so there is
nothing here that could be returned honestly: the plaintext would defeat the
encryption, and the ciphertext would be a value no caller can use.

Secrets are still usable without being readable: a configuration document
referencing `${{ NAME }}` resolves against the decrypted value when it is
served.

secret.description: Always `true`. A non-secret variable is returned as a bare scalar instead.

variable.title: Variable
variable.description:
One resolved variable. A non-secret variable is its value; a secret is an
object saying so and withholding the value.

The two forms mirror the update body, so a value read here can be written
back unchanged — with the one asymmetry that a secret read back has no value
to write.

variable-by-kind.title: VariableByKind
variable-by-kind.description: One variable's values, per kind. A kind with no value is absent.

variables-by-kind.title: VariablesByKind
variables-by-kind.description:
The project's variables, keyed by name, each with its value per kind.

An empty object is an ordinary answer, not an error.

secret-variable-input.title: SecretVariableInput
secret-variable-input.description:
A variable written with its secrecy stated explicitly.

Use this form to enter a secret. `{"value": "s3cr3t", "secret": true}` is
stored encrypted with the project's active `secret` key and
never reads back; the bare-scalar form is the same write with
`secret: false`.

secret.description:
Whether the value is stored encrypted. Changing it on an existing name
re-writes the value under the new flag — the documents referencing that
name do not change, because secrecy is a property of the value, not of
the reference to it.

variable-input.title: VariableInput
variable-input.description:
One entry of an update. A bare scalar enters a non-secret value, an object
states the flag explicitly, and `null` removes the name.

The shorthand exists because most variables are not secrets and spelling
`{"value": …, "secret": false}` for each of them is noise. Making a value
secret is therefore always deliberate: it cannot happen by writing a plain
scalar.

`null` is the RFC 7386 merge-patch convention: the name is removed, which is
what lets one request enter, replace and remove names together. Removing a
name the project does not hold is not an error, because a patch states what
the project holds afterwards and that name is already absent. `DELETE /variables/{variable_name}`
addresses one name deliberately and still answers `var.not_found` there.

A null is a removal wherever it appears, so a body built from client state in
which an unset field serializes to `null` removes that variable instead of
leaving it alone. A secret removed this way cannot be recovered, since its
value reads back nowhere. Send only the names the request means to change.

update-variables-request.title: UpdateVariablesRequest
update-variables-request.description:
The variables to enter, keyed by name. Each is either a bare scalar (a
non-secret value), an object stating the `secret` flag, or `null` to remove
the name.

This is a patch: a name present here is written, replacing whatever the
project held under it, and a name absent here is left alone. A name whose
value is `null` is removed (RFC 7386), so one request can enter, replace and remove names together —
which is also the way to remove several at once. `DELETE
/variables/{variable_name}` remains the way to remove exactly one name and
be told whether it was there.

Removing a name the project does not hold is not an error: a patch states
what the project holds afterwards, and that name is already absent. That makes a
retry safe, and it is the one place this body differs from `DELETE`, which
answers `var.not_found`.

The body is applied whole or not at all. Every value is validated, and every
secret encrypted, before anything is written, and the writes and removals
share one transaction.

The name of the variable is invalid

Error code: var.invalid_name

var-invalid_value.description:
The value of the variable is invalid

Error code: var.invalid_value

var-no_project_id.description:
A variable must be owned by a project

Error code: var.no_project_id

var-limit_exceeded.description:
The variables of this kind would not fit in one deployment

deployment-expand.description:
A related object to embed on each returned deployment.

- `release`: the release this deployment made live, as `release` on each
  deployment — the same representation `GET /releases/{release_id}` serves.
  The property is omitted entirely when not requested, so "did not ask" is
  distinguishable from asked-for content. One release per deployment, so no
  cap and no truncation flag.

  Requires `release.read` in addition to `deployment.read`.

deployment-kind.title: DeploymentKind
deployment-kind.description: `primary` for the project's primary origins, `preview` for preview URLs.

deployment-target.title: DeploymentTarget
deployment-target.description: One origin a deployment made its release live on.

expires_at.description:
Preview URLs only: the expiry this deployment set. A later deployment
to the URL records its own.

deployment-status.title: DeploymentStatus
deployment-status.description:
Whether the deployment serves its release now.

- `live` — at least one of its targets serves it now.
- `inactive` — none does: a later deployment replaced it, or its previews
  expired or were removed.

deployment-reason.title: DeploymentReason

deployment-metadata.title: DeploymentMetadata
deployment-metadata.description: Why the release went live and who made it happen.

message.description:
The caller-supplied summary of why this deployment happened, analogous
to a git commit message.

rollback_to.description: The deployment the rollback operation re-applied; null otherwise.

deployed_by.description:
The identity that created the deployment. Null when the caller is a
machine principal carrying no user identity, as from CI.

deployment.title: Deployment
deployment.description:
An immutable record of a release made live on a set of targets. Deploying
and rolling back each append one, so the history is the audit trail.

All primary origins serve the project's newest primary deployment; one
added after it serves nothing until the next deployment to `primary`. A
preview URL serves the newest deployment to it while its preview is live.

Every field is fixed at creation except `status`, which is read as of now.

id.description: The opaque, immutable resource id, assigned at creation.

project_id.description: The project this deployment belongs to.

release_id.description:
The release this deployment made live. Always the release id, also
when the request named the release by `content_hash`.

targets.description:
The resolved origins, sorted. For `primary`, the project's primary
origins at creation. The live view lists only the targets still served.

release.description:
The release named by `release_id`, present only when the request asked
for it with `expand: ["release"]` — the same representation
`GET /releases/{release_id}` serves. Absent means it was not requested.

list-deployments-response.description: One page of deployments, ordered as the operation describes.

next_page_token.description:
Token to pass as `page_token` in the next request to fetch the following page.
Absent when there are no more results.

deployment-targets-request.title: DeploymentTargetsRequest
deployment-targets-request.description:
Where the release goes live: either `primary`, which resolves to every
current primary origin, or preview URLs in `Origin` form, each matching one
of the project's preview patterns. Primary origins cannot be named one by
one, and the two forms cannot be mixed.

preview-ttl.title: PreviewTTL
preview-ttl.description:
How long a preview stays live after the deployment that writes it, as an
ISO-8601 duration. At most 365 days (`P365D`).

create-deployment-request.title: CreateDeploymentRequest
create-deployment-request.description:
The release to make live, named by exactly one of `release_id` or
`content_hash`, and the targets to make it live on.

content_hash.description:
The content digest of the release to make live, in full with its
`sha256:` prefix.

ttl.description:
Preview URLs only. How long each preview stays live from this
deployment; omitted, 7 days (`P7D`).

reason.description: Why this deployment happens. Omitted, the server records `deploy`.

message.description:
A short free-form summary of why this deployment happened, recorded on
its metadata.

expected_deployment_id.description:
Deploy only if the deployment this write replaces — the project's
newest primary deployment, or the newest deployment to any of the
preview URLs — is this one. Otherwise the request fails with
`409 dep.conflict` and nothing changes. Not stored.

dep-conflict.description:
Deployment: the deployment it replaces does not match expected_deployment_id

Error code: dep.conflict

dep-variables_missing.description:
Deployment: the release references variables its kind has no value for

Error code: dep.variables_missing

var-document_too_deep.description:
Variable: document nests too deeply

Error code: var.document_too_deep

deployment-variables-missing.title: DeploymentVariablesMissing
deployment-variables-missing.description: The release references variables the project holds no value for.

kind.description: The kind whose variable values the deployment would freeze.

names.description:
Every variable the release references with no value stored for
that kind, sorted.

create-deployment-bad-request.title: CreateDeploymentBadRequest
create-deployment-bad-request.description:
The deployment cannot be made, told apart by `code`; `req.invalid` is a
request the schema rejects.

deployment-guard-conflict.title: DeploymentGuardConflict
deployment-guard-conflict.description: `expected_deployment_id` is not the deployment this write replaces.

deployment.description:
The deployment this write replaces, null when there is none. Retry
with its id as `expected_deployment_id`.

release-revoked-conflict.title: ReleaseRevokedConflict
release-revoked-conflict.description: The release is revoked and cannot be deployed.

deployment-conflict.title: DeploymentConflict
deployment-conflict.description:
The deployment conflicts with the project, told apart by `code`:
`dep.conflict` (guard mismatch) or `rel.revoked`.

rollback-deployment-request.title: RollbackDeploymentRequest
rollback-deployment-request.description:
What to record alongside the rollback; the release, variable values and
targets are not chosen here.

message.description:
A short free-form summary of why the rollback happened. Recorded on
the new deployment's metadata.

expected_deployment_id.description:
Roll back only if the project's newest primary deployment is this one.
Otherwise the request fails with `409 dep.conflict` and nothing
changes. Not stored.

variables.description:
The variables a deployment froze, keyed by name.

The project the caller signs its users in to. The cookie's session is used
only when it belongs to this project; a session of any other project answers

A session belongs to one project, while a browser sends its cookie to every
app on the same host. An app passes its own project, so that a session of
another project never reads or acts as one of its users, and signing out of
the app never ends it. The SDKs pass it when they read the session or sign

its own project, so keep its cookie.

The cookies this response sets, one `Set-Cookie` line per element; the
generated server emits the lines separately, since the comma-joined form
OpenAPI prescribes for array headers is invalid for `Set-Cookie`
(RFC 6265). Browsers never expose the header to script, so this shape
concerns server-side and generated non-browser clients only.

Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/. Starting a flow and every submit
response rotate it, including validation failures; `GET /flow/{id}`
sets it only when the render resolved a parked SSO identity. The
`sso-redirect` response appends the browser-binding cookie the callback
checks.
